raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

A DCP transfer thread starts on CUDA device 0. When it packs rows for a P/D transfer, `torch.cuda.stream(...)` first records the current stream of device 0, which creates an unused CUDA context there. Every rank whose staging buffer lives on another GPU does this, so on an 8-GPU prefill sending to a decode with a larger DCP size, GPU 0 holds seven extra contexts and less usable memory than the other ranks. Packed bytes are not affected.

Found while running P/D with DCP relayout for Kimi-K3 serving.

## Modifications

- `try_pack_dcp_src` selects the staging buffer's device before the gather stream is used. The empty and over-capacity fallbacks still return first.
- Add `test_pd_dcp_pack_device.py`, a GPU test that packs from a fresh thread in a fresh process on device 0 and on device 1, checking the packed bytes and guard bytes against a CPU reference and which GPUs hold a context. The existing CPU test `test_dcp_pack.py` now mocks the device selection.

Verified [2ae31e9a73](https://github.com/Venkat2811/sglang/commit/2ae31e9a73186a3421c7fcbf0d16b1f9e2608e43) against parent [44be30d216](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/commit/44be30d2165318011fa1e9002cf58d6061907ed4) on one node with eight B300 GPUs:

| Check | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GPU test, `test_pd_dcp_pack_device.py` | Device 0 passes; device 1 fails: contexts on GPUs 0 and 1 | Both pass: context on the owning GPU only |
| CPU test, `test_dcp_pack.py` (11 tests) | 1 error (no device selection) | 11 pass |
| Seven fresh workers on GPUs 1 to 7 | 7 contexts on GPU 0, 4,312 MiB | None on GPU 0 |
| Packed bytes (all workers) | Identical | Identical |
| Pack call from a transfer thread, 54 MiB, three fresh runs | Median 196.2 to 201.8 µs | Median 191.3 to 195.1 µs |

## Accuracy Tests

The gather kernel is unchanged. In both arms the packed bytes and guard bytes match a CPU reference, and every worker produces the same SHA-256. No model output can change.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

The pack call is not slower: medians of 191.3 to 195.1 µs after against 196.2 to 201.8 µs before, 200 calls per run after 20 warm-up calls, 24 layers × 576 bytes × 4,096 tokens per call. The fix runs once per pack call and adds no synchronization.

Environment: driver 580.178.04, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130. The CPU and GPU tests ran through SGLang's CI runner and unittest; pre-commit passes on all three changed files. Hosted CI has not run yet.

<details>
<summary>Reproduce: correctness, memory and speed, before and after</summary>

Needs one node with at least two GPUs (eight for the memory check) and a CUDA SGLang environment.

```bash
git clone --single-branch --branch codex/dcp-pack-thread-device-2026-10-15 \
  https://github.com/Venkat2811/sglang.git sglang-dcp-pack
cd sglang-dcp-pack
git checkout 2ae31e9a73186a3421c7fcbf0d16b1f9e2608e43
export PYTHONPATH="$PWD/python:$PWD"

# Correctness and device selection
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1 python test/registered/kernels/ops/kvcache/test_pd_dcp_pack_device.py -v
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 python test/registered/unit/disaggregation/test_dcp_pack.py -v

# Memory: seven fresh workers on GPUs 1 to 7 (save measure_contexts.py below)
python measure_contexts.py test/registered/kernels/ops/kvcache/test_pd_dcp_pack_device.py 7

# Speed (save bench_pack.py below)
python bench_pack.py

# Before: restore the parent's runtime file, keep the new tests, rerun the same commands
git checkout 44be30d2165318011fa1e9002cf58d6061907ed4 -- python/sglang/srt/disaggregation/common/dcp_pack.py
```

Expected output of the memory check, before: `"gpu0_contexts": 7`; after: `"gpu0_contexts": 0`; `"identical_packed_bytes": true` in both.

`measure_contexts.py`

```python
"""Start one fresh process per GPU 1..N that packs from a transfer thread; report the GPUs each process holds."""
import json, pathlib, subprocess, sys, tempfile, time

test, n = sys.argv[1], int(sys.argv[2]) if len(sys.argv) > 2 else 7
tmp = pathlib.Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
procs = []
for d in range(1, n + 1):
    code = (
        f"import json, pathlib, runpy, time; "
        f"r = runpy.run_path({test!r})['_pack_in_fresh_thread']({d}); "
        f"pathlib.Path({str(tmp / f'{d}.json')!r}).write_text(json.dumps(r)); "
        f"[time.sleep(0.1) for _ in iter(pathlib.Path({str(tmp / 'release')!r}).exists, True)]"
    )
    procs.append(subprocess.Popen([sys.executable, "-c", code]))
while not all((tmp / f"{d}.json").exists() for d in range(1, n + 1)):
    assert all(p.poll() is None for p in procs), "a worker exited early"
    time.sleep(0.2)
smi = lambda *a: subprocess.check_output(["nvidia-smi", *a], text=True)
gpu0 = smi("-i", "0", "--query-gpu=uuid", "--format=csv,noheader").strip()
pids = {p.pid for p in procs}
rows = [r.split(", ") for r in smi("--query-compute-apps=pid,gpu_uuid,used_memory", "--format=csv,noheader,nounits").splitlines()]
mine = [r for r in rows if int(r[0]) in pids]
on0 = [r for r in mine if r[1] == gpu0]
hashes = {json.loads((tmp / f"{d}.json").read_text())["buffer_sha256"] for d in range(1, n + 1)}
print(json.dumps({"workers": n, "worker_contexts": len(mine), "gpu0_contexts": len(on0),
                  "gpu0_MiB": sum(int(r[2]) for r in on0), "identical_packed_bytes": len(hashes) == 1}))
(tmp / "release").touch()
for p in procs:
    p.wait()
```

`bench_pack.py`

```python
"""Median time of one DCP pack call from a transfer thread on GPU 1 (24 MLA layers x 576 B x 4,096 tokens)."""
import statistics, threading, time
import numpy as np, torch
from sglang.srt.disaggregation.common.dcp_pack import try_pack_dcp_src
from sglang.srt.disaggregation.common.staging_buffer import StagingBuffer

dev, layers, width, pool, tokens = 1, 24, 576, 8192, 4096
torch.cuda.set_device(dev)
sources = [torch.randint(0, 256, (pool, width), dtype=torch.uint8, device=f"cuda:{dev}") for _ in range(layers)]
buffer = StagingBuffer(layers * width * tokens, f"cuda:{dev}", dev)
indices = np.random.default_rng(0).choice(pool, tokens, replace=False).astype(np.int64)
kwargs = dict(pack_buffer=buffer, kv_data_ptrs=[s.data_ptr() for s in sources], token_item_lens=[width] * layers,
              src_token_item_lens=[width] * layers, pack_offset_bytes=0, src_token_indices=indices)
times = []

def worker():
    for i in range(220):
        t = time.perf_counter()
        assert try_pack_dcp_src(**kwargs) is not None
        if i >= 20:
            times.append((time.perf_counter() - t) * 1e6)

thread = threading.Thread(target=worker)
thread.start()
thread.join()
print(f"pack median {statistics.median(times):.1f} us, p90 {sorted(times)[int(0.9 * len(times))]:.1f} us over {len(times)} calls, {layers * width * tokens / 2**20:.1f} MiB per call")
```

</details>

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). No user-facing change; no documentation update needed.
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

+"""Exercise a transfer thread in a fresh process, before device 0 has a context."""
+
+import hashlib
+import subprocess
+import sys
+import threading
+import unittest
+from pathlib import Path
+
+import numpy as np
+import torch
+
+from sglang.srt.disaggregation.common.dcp_pack import try_pack_dcp_src
+from sglang.srt.disaggregation.common.staging_buffer import StagingBuffer
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cuda_ci
+
+register_cuda_ci(est_time=25, stage="base-b", runner_config="2-gpu-large")
+
+
+def _pack_in_fresh_thread(device_index):
+    def active_contexts():
+        return [
+            i
+            for i in range(torch.cuda.device_count())
+            if torch._C._cuda_hasPrimaryContext(i)
+        ]
+
+    assert active_contexts() == [], "Run this check in a fresh process"
+    device = torch.device("cuda", device_index)
+    torch.cuda.set_device(device)
+    # Independent random bytes distinguish rows, layers, and source padding.
+    rng = np.random.default_rng(71015)
+    widths = [576, 1152, 513]
+    strides = [576, 1168, 544]
+    cpu_sources = [rng.integers(0, 256, (67, s), np.uint8) for s in strides]
+    sources = [torch.from_numpy(x).to(device) for x in cpu_sources]
+    indices = np.array([66, 0, 9, 32, 1, 63, 9], dtype=np.int64)
+    required = len(indices) * sum(widths)
+    offset = 13
+    buffer = StagingBuffer(offset + required + 19, str(device), device_index)
+    buffer.buffer.fill_(165)
+    torch.cuda.synchronize(device)
+    before = active_contexts()
+    assert before == [device_index], before
+    results = {}
+    errors = []
+
+    def worker():
+        try:
+            kwargs = dict(
+                pack_buffer=buffer,
+                kv_data_ptrs=[x.data_ptr() for x in sources],
+                token_item_lens=widths,
+                src_token_item_lens=strides,
+                pack_offset_bytes=offset,
+            )
+            # Empty/overflow fallbacks must not initialize any other device.
+            empty = try_pack_dcp_src(
+                src_token_indices=np.array([], dtype=np.int64), **kwargs
+            )
+            assert empty[0] == [] and empty[1].size == 0
+            assert (
+                try_pack_dcp_src(
+                    src_token_indices=indices,
+                    pack_capacity_bytes=required - 1,
+                    **kwargs,
+                )
+                is None
+            )
+            results["fallback_contexts"] = active_contexts()
+            for _ in range(2):
+                # Exercise lazy stream construction and reuse on the same thread.
+                ptrs, dense_indices = try_pack_dcp_src(
+                    src_token_indices=indices, **kwargs
+                )
+                np.testing.assert_array_equal(dense_indices, np.arange(len(indices)))
+                expected_ptrs = []
+                cursor = buffer.get_ptr() + offset
+                for width in widths:
+                    expected_ptrs.append(cursor)
+                    cursor += len(indices) * width
+                assert ptrs == expected_ptrs, (ptrs, expected_ptrs)
+            results["thread_device_after"] = torch.cuda.current_device()
+        except BaseException as error:
+            errors.append(error)
+
+    thread = threading.Thread(target=worker, daemon=True)
+    thread.start()
+    thread.join(90)
+    assert not thread.is_alive(), "Transfer thread timed out"
+    if errors:
+        raise errors[0]
+    expected = np.full(buffer.get_size(), 165, dtype=np.uint8)
+    expected[offset : offset + required] = np.concatenate(
+        [x[indices, :width].reshape(-1) for x, width in zip(cpu_sources, widths)]
+    )
+    actual = buffer.buffer.cpu().numpy()
+    np.testing.assert_array_equal(actual, expected)
+    return {
+        **results,
+        "device": device_index,
